context:
Do the physical move first as a no-logic-change relocation (w1), add the
compat shim immediately after (w2) so nothing breaks mid-migration, then
update the real importers in core/ and platforms/ (w3) to point at the new
location so the dependency graph is actually fixed - the shim alone does
not fix layering, only the updated importers do. Treat the public-contract
question (w4) as a documentation/deprecation-window decision, not a design
blocker for the move itself.
description:
Architecture review (Work Area E, structural remediation) found a layering
inversion: nine `benchbox/core/*/benchmark.py` modules import
`benchbox.cli.benchmark_hooks` at module level - e.g.
`benchbox/core/nyctaxi/benchmark.py:643`,
`benchbox/core/tpcdi/benchmark.py:2743`,
`benchbox/core/datavault/benchmark.py:477` (confirmed 10 importing modules
total: flightdata, tsbs_devops, tpcdi, nyctaxi, datavault, tpcds_obt,
vector_search, joinorder_synthetic, joinorder, tpch_skew) - and
`benchbox/platforms/__init__.py:593` imports `benchbox.cli.platform_hooks`,
which itself imports `benchbox.core.platform_registry` and
`benchbox.core.schemas` (`cli/platform_hooks.py:13-14`).

Both `benchbox/cli/benchmark_hooks.py` and `benchbox/cli/platform_hooks.py`
are dependency-free (or near-dependency-free) pure registries - lightweight
extension mechanisms letting benchmarks/platforms expose CLI option hooks
(`--benchmark-option K=V`) without changing core CLI code. Despite the
name/location, neither module actually depends on CLI parsing, click/argparse,
or terminal I/O; they are data-holding registries that `core/` and
`platforms/` should be able to depend on without reaching "up" into `cli/`.
Having `core -> cli` and `platforms -> cli` edges inverts the intended
`utils < core < platforms < cli` layering that `import-layering-enforcement`
(a separate TODO) will formalize.

This is a standalone structural fix, not a shrink-campaign item -
`_project/goal-shrink-core-code.md` scopes god-class/architecture
decompositions out of the autonomous shrink loop.

anti_patterns.dont: change registry class names, method signatures, or hook registration order during the move
anti_patterns.why: this is a location fix, not a redesign.

anti_patterns.dont: silently drop the cli.* shim without checking docs/reference/public-contracts.md first
anti_patterns.why: these may be documented as public import paths.

anti_patterns.dont: update core/platforms importers to the new location without first adding the cli/ shim
anti_patterns.why: a partially migrated state would break external callers still using the old cli.* path during the same PR window.

preserves.behavior: All 10 core benchmark modules and platforms/__init__.py continue to register their hooks at the same point in the import/registration sequence.
CLI --benchmark-option and platform-option parsing behavior (PlatformHookRegistry, PlatformOptionSpec, parse_bool, BenchmarkOptionError) is byte-identical after the move.
Existing imports of benchbox.cli.benchmark_hooks / benchbox.cli.platform_hooks from any external caller keep working via the shim for at least one release.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/cli/benchmark_hooks.py header comment ('Mirrors the platform_hooks.py pattern') - both registries already share a design pattern; relocate them together rather than one at a time to avoid a half-migrated state.

remove-or-integrate-legacy-cudf-platform-module.yaml - existing example of a relocation TODO in this same planning set that adds back-compat notes and a docs update step; follow its w0 (verify importers)/decide/update-docs shape.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -k 'benchmark_hooks or platform_hooks or cli_options' --tb=short
verifications.description: All benchmark and platform CLI option hooks still work after relocation

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c 'from benchbox.cli.benchmark_hooks import BenchmarkOptionError; from benchbox.cli.platform_hooks import PlatformHookRegistry; print("ok")'
verifications.description: Old cli.* import paths still resolve via the shim

verifications.command: grep -rn 'cli.benchmark_hooks\|cli.platform_hooks\|cli import benchmark_hooks\|cli import platform_hooks' benchbox/core benchbox/platforms
verifications.description: No remaining core/platforms module imports benchbox.cli.* for hooks
verifications.expected: no matches (only benchbox/cli/*.py shim files reference the old names, if any)

work_units.notes:
Used benchbox/core/hooks/ (not a top-level benchbox/hooks/) per the
default in open_questions - platforms consuming a core-owned registry
is consistent with utils < core < platforms < cli. Copied both files
byte-identical (verified with `diff`) into
benchbox/core/hooks/{benchmark_hooks,platform_hooks}.py plus a new
benchbox/core/hooks/__init__.py package docstring. All public names
(BenchmarkOptionError, BenchmarkOptionSpec, BenchmarkHookRegistry,
PlatformOptionError, PlatformOptionSpec, PlatformHookRegistry,
parse_bool, parse_int, parse_int_list, parse_str_list,
parse_enum_list, parse_datetime) preserved verbatim.
work_units.summary: Move benchmark_hooks.py and platform_hooks.py to benchbox/core/hooks/

work_units.notes:
benchbox/cli/benchmark_hooks.py and benchbox/cli/platform_hooks.py are
now thin re-export shims from benchbox.core.hooks.* with explicit
__all__ matching the original modules' __all__ (parse_bool stays
importable-but-not-in-__all__ for platform_hooks, matching prior
behavior). Checked docs/reference/public-contracts.md and
docs/reference/backward-compatibility.md - neither documented
benchbox.cli.benchmark_hooks/platform_hooks as public surface, so this
is an internal-only courtesy shim, not a documented deprecation
window. Added a row to backward-compatibility.md's Current Inventory
table noting the relocation and the shim's courtesy (non-guaranteed)
status per w4.
work_units.summary: Add back-compat import shims in benchbox/cli/ for one release

work_units.notes:
Updated all 10 core/*/benchmark.py importers (flightdata,
tsbs_devops, tpcdi, nyctaxi, datavault, tpcds_obt, vector_search,
joinorder_synthetic, joinorder, tpch_skew) plus 5 benchbox/platforms/*
importers (platforms/__init__.py:593, trino.py, presto.py,
base/config_utils.py, influxdb/__init__.py - a wider set than the
review's single named platforms/__init__.py:593 line, found via the
full-tree grep the TODO asked for) to import from
benchbox.core.hooks.benchmark_hooks / benchbox.core.hooks.platform_hooks
directly. Left all other benchbox/cli/* internal callers
(orchestrator.py, benchmarks.py, commands/run.py, help.py,
database.py, platform_defaults.py, main.py) importing the old
cli.* path unchanged - out of this TODO's scope_limit (only
cli/benchmark_hooks.py and cli/platform_hooks.py are modifiable
within cli/) and harmless since cli->cli via the shim isn't a
layering violation. Verified with
`grep -rn 'cli.benchmark_hooks\|cli.platform_hooks\|...' benchbox/core benchbox/platforms`
returning zero matches (after clearing __pycache__ and rewording the
new package's docstring so it doesn't itself match the grep pattern).
work_units.summary: Update all core/platforms importers to the new location

work_units.notes:
Neither module is listed in docs/reference/public-contracts.md, so
treated as internal-only. Added a Current Inventory row to
docs/reference/backward-compatibility.md documenting the shim as an
internal courtesy (not a guaranteed compatibility window) rather than
following the public deprecation-window process.
work_units.summary: Note the public-contract question and update docs if needed
